summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma and recent E. coli bacteremia and C. difficile infection, was admitted for altered mental status characterized by confusion, word repetition, and impaired cognition. Initial concerns included stroke or seizure, but MRI and EEG showed no acute intracranial pathology or epileptiform activity. Delirium was diagnosed, likely unmasked by the cumulative stress of cancer, chemotherapy, infection, and medications. He was started on olanzapine, which improved his mental status. Blood cultures remained negative, and he completed a course of IV antibiotics for bacteremia and oral vancomycin for C. diff. Atenolol and terazosin were held due to potential contribution to confusion. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged home with home infusion therapy, oral antibiotics, and a short course of olanzapine, with follow-up planned.
